assets.title: The Argument That Ends the War
assets.content:
# The Argument That Ends the War
*Why "just ask for help" keeps failing - and what replaces it.*

## What is actually happening

You are not failing at sleep. You are running an unowned shift. A newborn wakes every night, but nobody agreed in advance whose turn it is - so every night is renegotiated by two exhausted adults, and the default quietly becomes: you own all of it.

That is why "can you help more?" produces a one-off gesture (one Saturday morning) instead of a system. A request creates a favour. A schedule creates a default.

## The one thing that changes it

> **The night does not need more goodwill. It needs an owner and a roster.**

A written night contract does three things a conversation cannot:

1. Removes the emotional labour of asking - the schedule asks, not you.
2. Gives your partner a named shift, not "help" - a status upgrade, not charity.
3. Makes your protected sleep block real by scheduling the milk hand-off in advance.

## Why the breastfeeding objection is real - and solvable

If you are breastfeeding, "sleep through the night" is not simply available to you. The contract does not pretend otherwise. It schedules a hand-off (a pumped bottle, or your partner brings the baby to you to feed and returns her to the crib) so that your block is real, not fictional.

## What this is not

This is an operating system for how two adults divide the night. It is not baby sleep training, and it is not a substitute for medical or mental-health care. When exhaustion is more than tiredness, stop and route out (see the rescue card).

Before you run any roster, both adults read and agree the **safety guardrails** in Tonight's Shift Chart - infant safe sleep, staying fully awake on shift, no earplugs or sleep aids on shift, and the rule that the baby always overrides the roster.

**Educational content - not medical, clinical, or mental-health advice.**

assets.title: Tonight's Shift Chart + Contract Templates
assets.content:
# Tonight's Shift Chart + Contract Templates
*Print or fill on screen. Aim: a named, written shift by tonight.*

## Template A - Breastfeeding-compatible split
| Block | Owner | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| 21:00-01:00 | Partner | Covers settle/soothe/nappy; brings baby to mother only to feed, then returns baby to crib |
| 01:00-05:00 | Mother | Feeds; partner stays "on call" for resettles and nappy |
| 05:00-08:00 | Partner | Takes baby; mother sleeps uninterrupted |

## Template B - Formula / expressed alternating
| Night | 22:00-03:00 | 03:00-08:00 |
|---|---|---|
| Odd | Partner | Mother |
| Even | Mother | Partner |

## Roster C - No partner available (support web)
| Slot | Person | Job |
|---|---|---|
| 06:00-09:00 | Relative / friend / paid help | Morning relief so mother sleeps |

## Safety guardrails - both adults read and agree before you sign

These are not optional. They are the boundary the whole system runs inside.

**1. Infant safety is paramount.** This contract controls adult coordination only - it does NOT override safe-sleep practice. The baby always sleeps on their back, on a firm, flat, separate surface (crib or bassinet), free of blankets, pillows, bumper pads, or soft toys, in line with World Health Organization (WHO) and paediatric guidance. If you are unsure what safe sleep looks like for your baby's age and stage, ask your paediatrician or midwife before you start a roster.

**2. The active shift manager stays fully awake.** Whoever is on shift must remain awake and alert while handling the baby. Never hold the baby in a bed, sofa, or armchair if there is any risk of falling asleep. If you feel unsafe from fatigue, use the emergency handoff immediately (see the Rescue Card).

**3. No earplugs or sleep aids on shift.** The parent on shift must NOT wear earplugs or headphones, or use any sleep-inducing aid - they must be able to hear and respond to the baby. The off-duty parent MAY use earplugs or white noise to protect their sleep - that is the point of the system.

**4. The baby always overrides the roster.** If the baby cannot be settled, or you are worried about feeding, illness, injury, breathing, or any unusual behaviour, assess the baby and follow your existing paediatric or clinical guidance, or seek help. Use the agreed phrase **"I need a handoff."** The roster pauses. Baby comes first.

Initial: ________ (Mother)     Initial: ________ (Partner / Helper)     Date: ____________

## Fill in tonight
- Chosen template: A / B / C
- Shift 1 owner: ______________ starts: ______ ends: ______
- Shift 2 owner: ______________ starts: ______ ends: ______
- Emergency override (what counts): ______________________________
- First script line sent to partner (from the Script Pack): ______________________________

## Sleep Banker (fairness ledger)
- 1 credit = covering a 3-5 hour night block so the other can sleep.
- 1 payback = a morning sleep-in or a 3-hour afternoon nap.
- Log every credit/debit. **Redeem within 7 days or resentment compounds.**

assets.title: Which Night Model Fits Us?
assets.content:
[[DECISION]]
TITLE: Which Night Model Fits Us?
SUB: One question at a time. Pick the template that matches your reality, then fill in the clock times.
START: START — Who is available at night?
ROUTE: ok | A partner is present and willing to hold a shift | Use Template A (breastfeeding-compatible split) or B (formula/expressed alternating) | Go to Tonight's Shift Chart.
ROUTE: urgent | A partner is present but resists the whole idea | Use Template A/B plus the Script Pack "trial it one week" framing | Start tonight with one named shift only.
ROUTE: ok | A partner works away or is often absent at night | Use Roster C (support web): schedule a relative, friend, or paid morning-relief slot | Book the slot tonight.
ROUTE: ok | No partner in the home at all | Use Roster C only; protect one morning block through your support web | Log what actually worked.
ROUTE: emergency | Exhaustion has stopped being "tired" - hopeless, intrusive thoughts, cannot function by day | Stop the planning. This is beyond a night plan. | See the rescue card and route to the verified shared crisis list (Nigeria 112 / MANI / SURPIN; UK 999 / Samaritans 116 123; US-Canada 911 / 988).
BAND: Educational coordination support - not a diagnosis. When in doubt about your mental health, seek professional care.
[[/DECISION]]

assets.title: Seven Script Cards
assets.content:
[[SCRIPTS]]
TITLE: Seven Script Cards
SUB: Ready words for the seven hardest moments. Calm, firm, no war.
SCRIPT: Opening the conversation (not a complaint) | I've been running every night on no sleep, and I don't want us to keep re-fighting this at 3am. I want us to agree a simple roster, tonight. I'll show you the two options - can we pick one before bed?
SCRIPT: "I have work tomorrow" | I know work is real. So is the fact that I've had no 3-hour block in weeks. This roster protects both of us: your work nights are planned, and I get one protected block. Let's run it for one week and review.
SCRIPT: "I don't hear the baby" | That's fair - you sleep deeply. So we don't rely on hearing. Your shift has an alarm, and I hand the baby over at a fixed time so it doesn't depend on you waking up.
SCRIPT: "You're breastfeeding, what can I do?" | You can take the resettles and nappies and hand her to me only for feeds, then put her back. That way my block is real even though I'm feeding.
SCRIPT: "My mother says this is your job" | I respect your mother. Our baby, our home, our roster. We're not asking her to run our nights.
SCRIPT: It broke last night (reset, no blame) | Last night didn't go to plan. That's a data point, not a failure. Let's just fix the alarm/handoff for tonight and keep going.
SCRIPT: When I feel the rage rise | I am exhausted, not broken. The roster exists so this doesn't land on him sideways. Tonight is his shift; I will sleep. If this feeling is more than tiredness, I will use the rescue card.
BAND: The pattern: honour the person -> state the rule once -> give them a role. You are not arguing; you are leading.
[[/SCRIPTS]]

assets.title: Bad Night Protocol + When Exhaustion Needs More
assets.content:
[[RESCUE]]
TITLE: BAD NIGHT PROTOCOL + WHEN EXHAUSTION NEEDS MORE
*If you are reading this at 3am because everything broke - start here.*

## Step 1 - Check the baby first
Before anything else, check the baby. If the baby has a fever, is vomiting, is showing signs of unusual pain, is having difficulty breathing, or you have any concern about their physical wellbeing - **suspend the roster** and follow your paediatric guidance, or contact emergency services:

- Nigeria **112** · United Kingdom **999** · US / Canada **911**

The roster never takes priority over the baby's health. It resumes when the baby is stable and you have appropriate support in place.

## When a night collapses
1. Default to whoever's turn it technically is.
2. The override triggers automatic next-night compensation (log it in the tracker).
3. Do not renegotiate the whole system at 3am. Just run the fallback.

## When the system keeps breaking
- Missed shift -> no-blame reset script; adjust the alarm/handoff method.
- Refusal -> use the "trial it for one week" framing from the Script Pack.
- Overwhelm -> simplify to ONE non-negotiable block; drop the rest temporarily.
- Relapse -> restart at the Negotiate step; no guilt.
- New helper arrives with old advice -> they read the shift chart before a night shift.

## When exhaustion needs more than a night plan
Severe, sustained exhaustion can mask or worsen postpartum mental-health conditions - and a better roster will not fix that. **This card cannot and does not diagnose anything.** It helps you recognise when something more is happening. Read this checklist honestly - for yourself, or for your partner:

- [ ] An overwhelming sense of hopelessness, emptiness, or sadness that does not lift even after a good sleep block.
- [ ] Intense anxiety, panic, or rapid heartbeats when thinking about the baby's sleep or night-time.
- [ ] Being unable to fall asleep even when the baby is sleeping and your partner is on duty.
- [ ] Intrusive, frightening thoughts of harm coming to yourself or the baby.
- [ ] Feeling disconnected from your baby, or feeling as though they would be better off without you.

**If you experience two or more of these, consistently, for more than two weeks, do not try to manage this with sleep schedules alone - seek professional assessment.** And if anything on this list is acute - thoughts of harm, feeling your baby would be better off without you, or physical symptoms that concern you (chest pain, fainting, uncontrolled bleeding, fever) - act today, not later. This is a clinical situation, not a scheduling one, and it is treatable.

Do not wait. Use the verified shared crisis/escalation list, routed in three tiers - **RED = emergency now · AMBER = urgent today · GREEN = supported this week**:

- **Nigeria** - Emergency **112** (toll-free, no airtime needed) or 199 · MANI 24/7 free confidential **0809 111 6264** or **0811 168 0686** · SURPIN 24/7 suicide/mental health **+234 806 210 6493**. Nigeria has no 988-style number.
- **United Kingdom** - Emergency **999** · Samaritans 24/7 **116 123**
- **United States & Canada** - Emergency **911** · Crisis Lifeline **988** (text HOME to 741741)

If you are in immediate danger, contact your local emergency number now.
[[/RESCUE]]

items.a: A postpartum night-coordination system: a written roster both adults follow, three contract templates, a sleep banker that makes invisible exhaustion tradeable, and the scripts to get a resistant partner on board - so the mother gets one protected 4-5 hour sleep opportunity most nights.

items.q: I'm breastfeeding - can this even work for me?
